name: Accumulation
subject: English Language
description: Piling up words or points one after another for force. “He was rude, loud, careless, cruel.”

name: Adynaton
subject: English Language
description: Hyperbole so extreme it says something is impossible. “When pigs fly.”

name: Allegory
subject: English Language
description: A story whose characters and events stand for something else — usually a moral or political idea.

name: Alliteration
subject: English Language
description: The same sound starting words close together. “The slow, sad song.”

name: Allusion
subject: English Language
description: A passing reference to something outside the text — a book, a myth, an event — without explaining it.

name: Amblysia
subject: English Language
description: Softening bad news before delivering it.

name: Amphiboly
subject: English Language
description: A sentence that can be read two ways because of how it is built, not because of a word’s meaning.

name: Anachronism
subject: English Language
description: Something in the wrong time period — a clock in a Roman play.

name: Anacoluthon
subject: English Language
description: A sentence that starts one way and finishes another, as speech often does.

name: Anadiplosis
subject: English Language
description: Ending a clause and starting the next with the same word. “Fear leads to anger, anger leads to hate.”

name: Analogue
subject: English Language
description: A thing that corresponds to another — a parallel drawn between two situations.

name: Anaphora
subject: English Language
description: The same words at the start of each line or clause. “We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight…”

name: Anastrophe
subject: English Language
description: Words put in an unusual order for effect. “Powerful you have become.”

name: Anecdote
subject: English Language
description: A short personal story used to make a point.

name: Anesis
subject: English Language
description: Ending with a detail that undercuts everything said before it.

name: Antagonist
subject: English Language
description: The character working against the protagonist.

name: Antanaclasis
subject: English Language
description: Repeating a word with a different meaning each time. “Put out the light, then put out the light.”

name: Anthropomorphism
subject: English Language
description: Giving an animal or object a human body or human behaviour — not just human feelings.

name: Anthimeria
subject: English Language
description: Using one part of speech as another. “I’ll text you” — a noun made a verb.

name: Antipophora
subject: English Language
description: Asking a question and immediately answering it yourself.

name: Antimetabole
subject: English Language
description: Repeating a phrase with the order reversed. “Ask not what your country can do for you…”

name: Antiphrasis
subject: English Language
description: Using a word to mean its opposite, usually sarcastically. Calling a giant “Tiny”.

name: Antithesis
subject: English Language
description: Two opposite ideas set against each other in a balanced way. “It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.”

name: Antonomasia
subject: English Language
description: Replacing a name with a description, or a description with a name. “The Bard” for Shakespeare.

name: Aphorism
subject: English Language
description: A short statement of a general truth. “Less is more.”

name: Aposiopesis
subject: English Language
description: Breaking off mid-sentence, leaving it unfinished. “If you don’t stop —”

name: Apostrophe
subject: English Language
description: Speaking directly to somebody absent, dead, or to an idea. “O Death, where is thy sting?”

name: Archaism
subject: English Language
description: An old-fashioned word or form used on purpose. “Thou”, “hither”.

name: Assonance
subject: English Language
description: The same vowel sound repeated in nearby words. “The rain in Spain.”

name: Asyndeton
subject: English Language
description: Leaving out the conjunctions to speed a list up. “I came, I saw, I conquered.”

name: Aside
subject: English Language
description: A remark to the audience the other characters cannot hear.

name: Bathos
subject: English Language
description: A sudden drop from the lofty to the ridiculous, usually by accident.

name: Black comedy
subject: English Language
description: Finding humour in things normally too grim to laugh at.

name: Blank verse
subject: English Language
description: Unrhymed lines in iambic pentameter — the usual line of Shakespeare’s plays.

name: Blazon
subject: English Language
description: Listing a person’s features one by one in praise, common in love poetry.

name: Bombast
subject: English Language
description: Language far grander than the subject deserves.

name: Burlesque
subject: English Language
description: Mocking something by treating a serious subject lightly, or a trivial one seriously.

name: Cacophony
subject: English Language
description: Harsh, clashing sounds put together on purpose.

name: Caesura
subject: English Language
description: A deliberate pause in the middle of a line of verse.

name: Catachresis
subject: English Language
description: A word used wrongly or a strained metaphor. “To take arms against a sea of troubles.”

name: Catalexis
subject: English Language
description: Dropping a syllable from the end of a line of verse.

name: Catharsis
subject: English Language
description: The release of emotion an audience feels at the end of a tragedy.

name: Chiasmus
subject: English Language
description: Ideas mirrored in an ABBA order. “Fair is foul, and foul is fair.”

name: Circumlocution
subject: English Language
description: Taking many words to say what could be said in few.

name: Cliché
subject: English Language
description: A phrase worn out by overuse. “At the end of the day.”

name: Conceit
subject: English Language
description: An extended, surprising comparison held across a whole poem.

name: Connotation
subject: English Language
description: What a word suggests beyond its plain meaning — “home” against “house”.

name: Consonance
subject: English Language
description: The same consonant sounds repeated, usually at the ends of words. “pitter patter”.

name: Couplet
subject: English Language
description: Two lines together, usually rhyming.

name: Cyclical ending
subject: English Language
description: An ending that returns to where the piece began.

name: Call to Action
subject: English Language
description: A direct instruction to the reader to do something. Common at the end of persuasive writing.

name: Defamiliarisation
subject: English Language
description: Describing an ordinary thing strangely so it is noticed again.

name: Denotation
subject: English Language
description: A word’s plain dictionary meaning, with nothing suggested on top.

name: Depitation
subject: English Language
description: Cutting a word short by removing its ending.

name: Dissonance
subject: English Language
description: Deliberately awkward, unmusical sound.

name: Double entendre
subject: English Language
description: A phrase with two meanings, one of them usually rude.

name: Dramatic irony
subject: English Language
description: The audience knows something a character does not.

name: Dysphemism
subject: English Language
description: A harsher word used where a neutral one would do — the opposite of a euphemism.

name: Direct Mode of address
subject: English Language
description: Speaking straight to the reader as “you”.

name: Ecphonema
subject: English Language
description: An exclamation — a sudden cry of emotion.

name: Ekphrasis
subject: English Language
description: A vivid description of a work of art inside a piece of writing.

name: Elegy
subject: English Language
description: A poem of mourning for somebody who has died.

name: Elision
subject: English Language
description: Leaving a sound out, usually to fit a rhythm. “o’er” for “over”.

name: Ellipsis
subject: English Language
description: Leaving words out, or the three dots that show it.

name: Emotive language
subject: English Language
description: Word choices picked to stir feeling rather than to inform.

name: Enjambment
subject: English Language
description: A sentence running over the end of a line of verse without a pause.

name: Epanados
subject: English Language
description: Repeating an idea in reverse order to expand on it.

name: Epanalepsis
subject: English Language
description: Beginning and ending a clause with the same word. “The king is dead, long live the king.”

name: Epexegesis
subject: English Language
description: Adding words to make an earlier phrase clearer.

name: Epideictic oratory
subject: English Language
description: Speech of praise or blame — a eulogy, a tribute.

name: Epistrophe
subject: English Language
description: The same word ending each clause — the opposite of anaphora.

name: Epitasis
subject: English Language
description: The part of a play where the action builds toward its climax.

name: Epizeuxis
subject: English Language
description: The same word repeated immediately, with nothing between. “Never, never, never.”

name: Euphemism
subject: English Language
description: A gentler phrase for something harsh. “Passed away.”

name: Euphony
subject: English Language
description: Sounds chosen because they are pleasant together.

name: Farce
subject: English Language
description: Comedy built on absurd situations and improbable coincidence.

name: Feminine rhyme
subject: English Language
description: A rhyme on two syllables, the last unstressed. “motion / ocean”.

name: Flyting
subject: English Language
description: A contest of insults, traded in verse.

name: Foil
subject: English Language
description: A character whose opposite qualities highlight another’s.

name: Frame Narrative
subject: English Language
description: A story told inside another story.

name: Flashback
subject: English Language
description: A scene that jumps back to an earlier time.

name: Foreshadowing
subject: English Language
description: A hint early on of what is to come.

name: Free verse
subject: English Language
description: Poetry with no fixed metre or rhyme scheme.

name: Hamartia
subject: English Language
description: The flaw or mistake that brings a tragic hero down.

name: Hemistich
subject: English Language
description: Half a line of verse, usually split by a pause.

name: Hendiadys
subject: English Language
description: One idea expressed as two nouns joined by “and”. “Sound and fury” for furious sound.

name: Homonym
subject: English Language
description: Words spelt and said the same with different meanings. “bat”.

name: Homophone
subject: English Language
description: Words that sound the same but are spelt differently. “there / their”.

name: Hubris
subject: English Language
description: Excessive pride, usually the thing that causes the fall.

name: Hypallage
subject: English Language
description: Swapping which word an adjective belongs to. “A sleepless night.”

name: Hyperbaton
subject: English Language
description: Words separated from the ones they belong with, for emphasis.

name: Hyperbole
subject: English Language
description: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally. “I’ve told you a thousand times.”

name: Hypocorism
subject: English Language
description: A pet name or affectionate diminutive.

name: Hypostatisation
subject: English Language
description: Treating an idea as though it were a real thing that can act.

name: Hypotyposis
subject: English Language
description: Description so vivid the scene seems to be in front of you.

name: Hypozeuxis
subject: English Language
description: Giving every clause its own subject and verb, for weight.

name: Idiom
subject: English Language
description: A phrase whose meaning cannot be worked out from its words. “Kick the bucket.”

name: Imagery
subject: English Language
description: Language that appeals to the senses to build a picture.

name: Invective
subject: English Language
description: Abusive, attacking language.

name: Inversion
subject: English Language
description: Reversing the normal word order. “Into the valley rode the six hundred.”

name: Invocation
subject: English Language
description: Calling on a muse or a god for help, usually at the start of an epic.

name: In media res
subject: English Language
description: Beginning in the middle of the action rather than at the start.

name: Irony
subject: English Language
description: Saying one thing and meaning another, or an outcome that is the opposite of what was expected.

name: Isocolon
subject: English Language
description: Clauses of matching length and structure. “Veni, vidi, vici.”

name: Juxtaposition
subject: English Language
description: Two things placed side by side so the contrast shows.

name: Jargon
subject: English Language
description: Specialist vocabulary belonging to a trade or group.

name: Kenning
subject: English Language
description: A compound phrase standing in for a noun. “Whale-road” for the sea.

name: Light rhyme
subject: English Language
description: A rhyme where one syllable is stressed and the other is not.

name: Litotes
subject: English Language
description: Understatement made by denying the opposite. “Not bad” for good.

name: Malapropism
subject: English Language
description: The wrong word used for one that sounds like it, comically. “Dance a flamingo.”

name: Masculine rhyme
subject: English Language
description: A rhyme on a single stressed syllable. “hand / stand”.

name: Meiosis
subject: English Language
description: Belittling something by describing it as far less than it is.

name: Melodrama
subject: English Language
description: Exaggerated emotion and sensational plot, characters drawn broadly.

name: Metalepsis
subject: English Language
description: A reference so indirect it needs a second leap to follow.

name: Metaphor
subject: English Language
description: Saying one thing IS another. “Time is a thief.”

name: Meter
subject: English Language
description: The pattern of stressed and unstressed syllables in a line.

name: Metonymy
subject: English Language
description: Naming something by a thing closely linked to it. “The Crown” for the monarchy.

name: Monologue
subject: English Language
description: One character speaking at length, alone or to others.

name: Motif
subject: English Language
description: An image or idea that recurs through a work and builds meaning.

name: Mythopoeia
subject: English Language
description: Making a myth — inventing a legend rather than retelling one.

name: Neologism
subject: English Language
description: A newly invented word.

name: Nonce-word
subject: English Language
description: A word coined for one occasion and not used again.

name: Onomatopoeia
subject: English Language
description: A word that sounds like the thing it names. “Buzz”, “crash”.

name: Oxymoron
subject: English Language
description: Two contradictory words together. “Bittersweet”, “deafening silence”.

name: Palilogy
subject: English Language
description: Immediate repetition of a word for emphasis.

name: Paradox
subject: English Language
description: A statement that contradicts itself and is still true. “Less is more.”

name: Paralipsis
subject: English Language
description: Drawing attention to something by saying you will not mention it.

name: Parallelism
subject: English Language
description: Matching grammatical structure across phrases or clauses.

name: Parataxis
subject: English Language
description: Short clauses set side by side without conjunctions.

name: Parenthesis
subject: English Language
description: An aside inserted into a sentence, in brackets or dashes.

name: Paronomasia
subject: English Language
description: A pun — wordplay on words that sound alike.

name: Pathetic fallacy
subject: English Language
description: Weather or landscape reflecting a character’s mood.

name: Periphrasis
subject: English Language
description: Using more words than needed — a roundabout way of naming something.

name: Personification
subject: English Language
description: Giving human qualities to something that is not human. “The wind whispered.”

name: Platitude
subject: English Language
description: A flat, obvious remark offered as though it were wisdom.

name: Polyptoton
subject: English Language
description: Repeating a word in different forms. “With eager feeding food doth choke the feeder.”

name: Polysyndeton
subject: English Language
description: Repeating conjunctions to slow a list down. “and… and… and…”

name: Prolepsis
subject: English Language
description: Treating a future event as though it had already happened.

name: Prodiorthosis
subject: English Language
description: Warning the audience that what comes next may shock them.

name: Protagonist
subject: English Language
description: The main character, whose choices drive the story.

name: Repartee
subject: English Language
description: Quick, witty reply — conversation as a duel.

name: Rhetorical question
subject: English Language
description: A question asked for effect, not for an answer.

name: Rhyme
subject: English Language
description: Matching sounds at the ends of words or lines.

name: Rhythm
subject: English Language
description: The beat of the language — how stresses fall as it is read.

name: Satire
subject: English Language
description: Using humour and exaggeration to criticise people or institutions.

name: Sentence structure
subject: English Language
description: How a sentence is built — short and blunt, or long and layered — and what that does.

name: Setting
subject: English Language
description: Where and when a piece takes place, and the mood that creates.

name: Simile
subject: English Language
description: Comparing with “like” or “as”. “As cold as stone.”

name: Statistics
subject: English Language
description: Numbers used as evidence to make an argument harder to argue with.

name: Stichomythia
subject: English Language
description: Rapid dialogue in single alternating lines, used in argument.

name: Stream of consciousness
subject: English Language
description: Writing that follows thought as it actually runs, unordered.

name: Symbolism
subject: English Language
description: An object standing for an idea beyond itself.

name: Synaesthesia
subject: English Language
description: Describing one sense in terms of another. “A loud shirt.”

name: Syncope
subject: English Language
description: Dropping a sound from the middle of a word. “ne’er”.

name: Synecdoche
subject: English Language
description: A part standing for the whole. “All hands on deck.”

name: Tapinosis
subject: English Language
description: Language that belittles its subject.

name: Tmesis
subject: English Language
description: Splitting a word and putting something inside it. “Abso-bloody-lutely.”

name: Theme
subject: English Language
description: The underlying idea a work keeps returning to.

name: Tone
subject: English Language
description: The attitude the writing takes toward its subject.

name: Topothesia
subject: English Language
description: A description of an imaginary place.

name: Triple (Rule of Three)
subject: English Language
description: Three items together, which is the number that sounds complete. “Life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness.”

name: Unreliable Narrator
subject: English Language
description: A narrator whose account cannot be trusted.

name: Verisimilitude
subject: English Language
description: The appearance of being true to life.

name: Voice
subject: English Language
description: The distinct personality that comes through in the writing.

name: Zeugma
subject: English Language
description: One word governing two others, often oddly. “She took her coat and her leave.”
